title: How to avoid AI workslop that wastes your reader’s time
dek: AI can make unfinished thinking look finished. Before sending a draft, check whether your reader has the facts, decisions and next steps they need.

title: How Can Customers Find Your Small Business on ChatGPT?
dek: Make your services clear, check crawler access and try realistic searches. Practical steps for small-business owners, without promises of guaranteed recommendations.

title: ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini: which one is best at what
dek: Our picks, job by job: Claude for long documents, ChatGPT for numbers and images, Gemini or Copilot for everyday office work. Researched, not tested.

title: Hosting Thanksgiving? One prompt gets you the menu, the timeline and the grocery list
dek: Give ChatGPT four facts about your kitchen and ask for a menu, an hour-by-hour plan and one grocery list sorted by aisle. Then check the turkey against USDA.

title: Turn last month's bank statement into a budget you'll actually keep
dek: Holiday spending starts this month. Strip out the personal details, paste in one statement, and get a budget built on how you actually spend.

title: Can AI type your invoices into a spreadsheet?
dek: We ran 24 invented invoices, including scans and handwriting, through an AI model and a rules script. AI read messy ones better but missed a bad total.

title: AI vs. simple rules for appointment and payment reminders
dek: We ran 30 made-up reminder records through a rules script and an AI model three times each. Rules got every routine case right.

title: We tested our AI readiness checklist on 12 made-up workflows
dek: We ran our readiness checklist on 12 invented workflows. It's a good brake and a poor compass.

title: We ran 30 invented customer inquiries through an AI follow-up assistant
dek: A 30-case synthetic test: stop checks passed, but one draft made unapproved promises.

title: Small-business lead follow-up automation: a blueprint
dek: A lifecycle map for capture, handoff, follow-up, and closure, with exceptions and stop conditions to write first.

title: AI agents are moving into your business apps
dek: Use an Agent Action Contract and a contractor test plan to decide what an assistant may read, draft, propose, and change.

title: How to evaluate an AI pilot: keep, fix, or stop

title: What data should you put into an AI tool?
dek: Use a green-yellow-red data framework and a pre-upload checklist before business information enters an AI workflow.

title: How to calculate the ROI of AI automation

title: AI vs. automation: when your small business actually needs AI

title: How to choose your first AI tool without wasting money

title: The small-business AI readiness checklist

title: 5 tasks your small business should automate before anything else
